text: A particle is projected with velocity $v_{0}$ along x-axis. A damping force is acting on the particle which is proportional to the square of the distance from the origin i.e. ma = $-$ $αx^{2}$. The distance at which the particle stops :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, speed of projection $= v_{0}$

Damping force, F = ma = $-$ $αx^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ a = $-$ $αx^{2} / m$

Also, $a=v\frac{dv}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow vdv=adx=-\frac{α}{m}x^{2}dx$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\int\limits _{v_{0}}^{v}vdv=\int\limits _{0}^{x}-\frac{α}{m}x^{2}dx$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{v^{2}}{2}\right )_{v_{0}}^{0}=-\frac{α}{m}\left (\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right )_{0}^{x}$

$\Rightarrow 0-v_{0}^{2}/2=-\frac{α}{m}\frac{x^{3}}{3}\Rightarrow x=\left (\frac{3m}{2}\frac{v_{0}^{2}}{α}\right )^{1/3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: An X-ray tube is operated at 1.24 million volt. The shortest wavelength of the produced photon will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, V = 1.24 million volt = 1.24 $\times$ $10^{6}$ volt

Since, energy (E) = eV

where, e is the charge of electron = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19} C$

$\therefore$ E = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19}$ $\times$ 1.24 $\times$ $10^{6} ..... (i)$

As we know that,

Energy of photon, $E=\frac{hc}{λ}$ .... (ii)

Here, Planck's constant, h = 6.67 $\times$ $10^{-34} J-s$,

c = speed of light in free space, c = 3 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}$

Equating Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 1.24\times 10^{6}=\frac{6.67\times 10^{-34}\times 3\times 10^{8}}{λ}$

$\Rightarrow λ=\frac{20.01\times 10^{-13}}{1.6\times 1.24}=10.09\times 10^{-13}$

$=1.009\times 10^{-12}\simeq 10^{-3}\times 10^{-9}$

$= 10^{-3} nm$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text:
If one mole of an ideal gas at $(P_{1}, V_{1})$ is allowed to expand reversibly and isothermally (A to B) its pressure is reduced to one-half of the original pressure (see figure). This is followed by a constant volume cooling till its pressure is reduced to one-fourth of the initial value (B $\to$ C). Then it is restored to its initial state by a reversible adiabatic compression (C to A). The net work done by the gas is equal to :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $p_{i}, p_{f}, V_{i}$ and $V_{f}$ be the initial and final pressure and volume.

Given, AB is isothermal ($\Delta$T = 0),

BC is isochoric ($\Delta$V = 0) and CA is adiabatic ($\Delta$Q = 0)

Since, isothermal work $(W_{AB}) =$ $p_{1}V_{1}\ln \frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}$


[IMG]

where, $V_{i}$ and $V_{f}$ are volume at A and B, respectively.

$\therefore$ $W_{AB}=p_{1}V_{1}\ln \frac{2V_{1}}{V_{1}}=p_{1}V_{1}\ln 2$

Since, at constant volume, work done is zero.

$\therefore$ $W_{BC}=0$

Since, $W_{CA}$ is an adiabatic work done, i.e.

$W_{CA}=\frac{1}{1-γ}(p_{f}V_{f}-p_{i}V_{i})$

$\Rightarrow W_{CA}=\frac{1}{1-γ}(p_{1}V_{1}-\frac{p_{1}}{4}\times 2V_{1})$

$=\frac{1}{1-γ}(p_{1}V_{1}-p_{1}V_{1}/2)=\frac{1}{1-γ}\frac{p_{1}V_{1}}{2}$

$\therefore$ Net work done, $W_{net}=W_{AB}+W_{BC}+W_{CA}$

$=p_{1}V_{1}\ln 2+0+\frac{1}{1-γ}\frac{p_{1}V_{1}}{2}$

$=p_{1}V_{1}[\ln 2+1/2(1-γ)]$

From ideal gas law, $pV=nRT$

$\therefore$ $W_{net}=RT[\ln 2-1/2(γ-1)]$ ($\because$ n = 1)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text:
A body weights 49N on a spring balance at the north pole. What will be its weight recorded on the same weighing machine, if it is shifted to the equator?

[Use $g=\frac{GM}{R^{2}}$ $= 9.8 ms^{-2}$ and radius of earth, R = 6400 km.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, weight of body at North pole,

$w_{p} = mg = 49 N$

Radius of Earth, R = 6400 km

Let weight of body at equator be $w_{e}$.

At equator, $g_{e} = g$ $-$ R$ω^{2}$

$\therefore$ $w_{e} = mg_{e} = m(g$ $-$ R$ω^{2}$)

Since, $w_{p} > w_{e}$ $\Rightarrow$ $w_{e} < 49 N$

Hence, above condition is satisfied by only option (c).

text: When a particle executes SHM, the nature of graphical representation of velocity as a function of displacement is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since, the particle is executing SHM.

Therefore, displacement equation of wave will be

$y=A\sin ωt$

$\Rightarrow y/A=\sin ωt$

and wave velocity equation will be

$v_{y}=\frac{dy}{dt}=Aω\cos ωt$

$\Rightarrow v_{y}/Aω=\cos ωt$

Now, $\sin ^{2}ωt+\cos ^{2}ωt=1$

$\therefore$ $(y/A)^{2}+(v_{y}/Aω)^{2}=1$

This equation is similar to the equation of ellipse.

text: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum is $T=2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$. Measured value of 'L' is 1.0 m from meter scale having a minimum division of 1 mm and time of one complete oscillation is 1.95 s measured from stopwatch of 0.01 s resolution. The percentage error in the determination of 'g' will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $T=2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$ .... (i)

where, time period, T = 1.95 s

Length of string, l = 1 m

Acceleration due to gravity = g

Error in time period, $\DeltaT = 0.01 s = 10^{-2} s$

Error in length, $\Delta$L = 1 mm = 1 $\times$ $10^{-3} m$

Squaring Eq. (i) on both sides, we get

$T^{2}=4π^{2}\frac{L}{g}$

$\Rightarrow g=4π^{2}\frac{L}{T^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta g}{g}=\frac{\Delta L}{L}+\frac{2\Delta T}{T}=\frac{10^{-3}}{1}+\frac{2\times 10^{-2}}{1.95}$

$=10^{-3}+1.025\times 10^{-2}$

$=10^{-3}+10.25\times 10^{-3}$

$=11.25\times 10^{-3}$

$\because$ $\Delta g/g\times 100=11.25\times 10^{-3}\times 10^{2}$

$=1.125%\simeq 1.13%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: Two electrons each are fixed at a distance '2d'. A third charge proton placed at the midpoint is displaced slightly by a distance x (x << d) perpendicular to the line joining the two fixed charges. Proton will execute simple harmonic motion having angular frequency : (m = mass of charged particle)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The arrangement of charges is shown below


[IMG]

As we know that,

Coulomb's force between two charges. $i.e., q_{1}$ and $q_{2}$,

$F=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\frac{q_{1}q_{2}}{r^{2}}=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\frac{q_{1}q_{2}}{(d^{2}+x^{2})}$ ..... (i)

Here, $q_{1}=q_{2}=q$

Force in SHM, $F=mω^{2}x$ ...... (ii)

Since, in order to have SHM +q should move downwards and force responsible for this will be only

$F^{'}=F\sin θ+F\sin θ=2F\sin θ$ ..... (iii)

Using Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get

$2F\sin θ=mω^{2}x$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{4πε_{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{(d^{2}+x^{2})}\sin θ=mω^{2}x$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{4πε_{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{(d^{2}+x^{2})}.\frac{x}{(d^{2}+x^{2})^{1/2}}=mω^{2}x$

$\Rightarrow ω=\left (\frac{1}{2πε_{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{(d^{2}+x^{2})^{3/2}m}\right )^{1/2}$

As, $x<<d$

$\therefore$ $ω=\left (\frac{1}{2πε_{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{md^{3}}\right )^{1/2}$

text: The de-Broglie wavelength of a proton and $α$-particle are equal. The ratio of their velocities is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $λ_{p}$, $λ_{α}$, $m_{p}, m_{α}, v_{p}, v_{α}, p_{p}$ and $p_{α}$ be the wavelength, mass, velocity and momentum of proton and $α$-particle, respectively.

Given, $λ_{p}$ = $λ_{α}$

As we know that,

$λ$ = h/p

$\therefore$ $\frac{h}{p_{p}}=\frac{h}{p_{α}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $p_{p} = p_{α}$

$\Rightarrow$ $m_{p}v_{p} = m_{α}v_{α}$

$\Rightarrow$ $m_{p}v_{p} = 4m_{p}v_{α} (\because$ $m_{α} = 4m_{p})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{v_{p}}{v_{α}}=\frac{4}{1}$ or 4 : 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: According to Bohr atomic model, in which of the following transitions will the frequency be maximum?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $n_{f}, n_{i}$ be the final and initial orbit.

As we know that,

$\frac{1}{λ}=1.09\times 10^{7}\left [\frac{1}{n_{f}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{i}^{2}}\right ]$

Now, checking for each option, we get

(a) $\frac{1}{λ}\propto \left [\frac{1}{3^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right ]=\left [\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{16}\right ]=0.05$ .... (i)

(b) $\frac{1}{λ}\propto \left [\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{4}\right ]=0.75$ .... (ii)

(c) $\frac{1}{λ}\propto \left [\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{25}\right ]=0.0225$ .... (iii)

(d) $\frac{1}{λ}\propto \left [\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right ]=0.14$ .... (iv)

The option (b) has highest value.

Since, frequency, $f=\frac{c}{λ}\Rightarrow f\propto \frac{1}{λ}$

$\therefore$ Frequency will be maximum for transition n = 2 to n = 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: A uniform metallic wire is elongated by 0.04 m when subjected to a linear force F. The elongation, if its length and diameter is doubled and subjected to the same force will be $________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let initial length and diameter be $l_{1}$ and $d_{1}$, whereas final length and diameter be $l_{2}$ and $d_{2}$.

Given, $l_{2} = 2l_{1}, d_{2} = 2d_{1}$, $\Deltal_{1} = 0.04 m$

By using formula of Young's modulus of elasticity,

$Y=\frac{F.l}{A\Delta l}$

$\therefore$ $Y_{1}=Y_{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{Fl_{1}}{A_{1}\times \Delta l_{1}}=\frac{Fl_{2}}{A_{2}\times \Delta l_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{Fl_{1}}{π(d_{1}/2)^{2}\times 0.04}=\frac{F2l_{1}}{π(2d_{1}/2)^{2}\times \Delta l_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{1/4\times 0.04}=\frac{2}{\Delta l_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \Delta l_{2}=0.02$ m = 2 cm

text: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 3 GHz enters a dielectric medium of relative electric permittivity 2.25 from vacuum. The wavelength of this wave in that medium will be $_________$ $\times$ $10^{-2} cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $f=3\text{GHz}=3\times 10^{9}\text{Hz}$ and $ε_{r}=2.25$. The dielectric is non-magnetic ($μ_{r}=1$), so its refractive index is $n=\sqrt{μ_{r}ε_{r}}=\sqrt{2.25}=1.5$.

Wavelength in vacuum:

$λ_{0}=\dfrac{c}{f}=\dfrac{3\times 10^{8}}{3\times 10^{9}}=0.1\text{m}=10\text{cm}$

The frequency does not change on entering the medium, so

$λ=\dfrac{λ_{0}}{n}=\dfrac{10}{1.5}=\dfrac{20}{3}\text{cm}=6.667\text{cm}=666.67\times 10^{-2}\text{cm}\approx 667\times 10^{-2}\text{cm}$

Hence, the answer is 667.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

Current flowing;

I = J $\times$ $πR^{2}$

I = 50 $\times$ $10^{4}$ $\times$ $π$(0.5 $\times$ $10^{-3})^{2}$

I = 50 $\times$ $10^{4}$ $\times$ $π$ $\times$ 0.25 $\times$ $10^{-6}$

I = 125 $\times$ $10^{-3}π$

$\therefore$ x = 5

text: Two solids A and B of mass 1 kg and 2 kg respectively are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their kinetic energies $(K.E.)_{A}$ : $(K.E.)_{B}$ will be $\frac{A}{1}$, so the value of A will be $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that, $\frac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$

Also, $p_{1} = p_{2} = p$

$\Rightarrow$ $M_{1}V_{1} = M_{2}V_{2} = p$

Also, we know that

$K=\frac{p^{2}}{2M}\Rightarrow K_{1}=\frac{p^{2}}{2M_{1}}$ & $K_{2}=\frac{p^{2}}{2M_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}=\frac{p^{2}}{2M_{1}}\times \frac{2M_{2}}{p^{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}=\frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}}=\frac{2}{1}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{A}{1}=\frac{2}{1}$ 

$\Rightarrow$ $\therefore$ A = 2

solution.body:
Given, $T_{1} = 27{}^{\circ }C = 27 + 273 = 300K, p_{1} = 1$ atm, $v_{1} = 200 ms^{-1}, T_{2} = 127{}^{\circ }C = 400 K, p_{2} = 2$ atm, $v_{2} =$ ?

As we know that,

Root mean square speed, $v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{m}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{300}{400}}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}$

$\Rightarrow v_{2}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}v_{1}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\times 200=\frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}$ $ms^{-1}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}\Rightarrow x=400$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift

text: A series L-C-R circuit is designed to resonate at an angular frequency $ω_{0}$ $= 10^{5}$ rad/s. The circuit draws 16W power from 120V source at resonance. The value of resistance 'R' in the circuit is $_________$ $\Omega$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, angular frequency at resonance, $ω_{0}$ $= 10^{5}$ rads$^{-1}$

Power drawn from circuit, P = 16 W

and supply voltage, V = 120 V

Let resistance of circuit = R.

As, $P=V^{2}/R$

$\Rightarrow R=V^{2}/P=\frac{120\times 120}{16}$

$=30\times 30=900\Omega$

text:
A point charge of +12$μ$C is at a distance 6 cm vertically above the centre of a square of side 12 cm as shown in figure. The magnitude of the electric flux through the square will be $__________$ $\times$ $10^{3} Nm^{2}/C$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, charge, q = 12 $μ$C = 12 $\times$ $10^{-6}C$
Height of charge from surface, h = 6 cm = 6 $\times$ $10^{-2} m$ and side of square, a = 12 cm = 12 $\times$ $10^{-2} m$

Using Gauss law, it is a part of cube of side 12 cm and charge at centre so;
$𝜙=\frac{Q}{6ε_{0}}=\frac{12μc}{6ε_{0}}=2\times 4π\times 9\times 10^{9}\times 10^{-6}$
$=226\times 10^{3}$ $Nm^{2} / C$

text: A uniform thin bar of mass 6 kg and length 2.4 meter is bent to make an equilateral hexagon. The moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of mass and perpendicular to the plane of hexagon is $_______$ $\times$ $10^{-1} kg m^{2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


MOI of AB about $P:I_{ABp}=\frac{\frac{M}{6}\left (\frac{l}{6}\right )^{2}}{12}$

MOI of AB about O, 

$I_{AB_{O}}=\left [\frac{\frac{M}{6}\left (\frac{l}{6}\right )^{2}}{12}+\frac{M}{6}\left (\frac{l}{6}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2}\right ]$

$I_{Hexagon_{0}}=6I_{AB_{0}}=M\left [\frac{l^{2}}{12\times 36}+\frac{l^{2}}{36}\times \frac{3}{4}\right ]$

$=\frac{6}{100}\left [\frac{24\times 24}{12\times 36}+\frac{24\times 24}{36}\times \frac{3}{4}\right ]$

= 0.8 kgm$^{2}$

= 8 $\times$ $10^{-1} kg-m^{2}$
